nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

products.opacity_note: Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.
products.annotation_reason: RYA-1213: the two new near-UV Fe I Reference Gerber-LTE rows landed after the previous annotation pass. Every near-UV product must state the band's residual opacity deficit or it reads as a converged answer.

nlte_capability.gerber_deck_ion_reach: Fe II: 58 levels, ZERO bound-bound transitions in atom.fe607a — an ionisation reservoir, not a term system. Fe I: 548 levels, 12,635 transitions.
nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: MPIA / Bergemann mafags-os 1D-NLTE per-line delta grid (data/nlte_grids/Fe_Bergemann_MPIA.csv) — NOT atom.fe607a. Its Fe II corrections are real and small: at the solar node the grid's Fe II deltas run -0.002 to +0.016 dex, median +0.000, with 146 of 160 entries inside +-0.005 (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). What THIS product actually applied is recorded per line in its own *_ENGINE-A_lines.csv (nlte_delta_dex / nlte_source, RYA-880); across every live Fe II product that is -0.001 to -0.002 dex, on the lines MPIA serves
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.
nlte_capability.deferred: a two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03)

nlte_capability.nlte_source_for_this_product: n/a — this product is on an LTE scale
nlte_capability.limit: Fe II NLTE unavailable on the Gerber deck: atom.fe607a carries 58 Fe II levels but ZERO Fe II bound-bound transitions (12,635 of 12,635 are Fe I -> Fe I), so bsyn applies departure = 1 to every Fe II line and no line list can enable it. Reported LTE. The effect is literature-negligible at solar -- Amarsi's grid gives -0.001 dex (vturb 0.75) and -0.0008 (1.50), and Lind et al. 2017 section 2.2.4 states 'For the Sun, NLTE effects on Fe II lines are insignificant' -- and our own MPIA/Bergemann Fe II deltas agree IN THE MEDIAN: +0.000 dex at the solar node, 146 of 160 grid entries inside +-0.005 -- though the tail is the three strong multiplet-42 lines 4923.932 / 4924.921 / 5169.033, all at +0.015 (max single grid entry +0.016), so 'negligible' is a median statement and not a bound (Fe I control at the same node: median +0.011, up to +0.040). A two-stage Fe atom is DEFERRED to the off-solar programme, where the Fe I/Fe II balance does the log g work (Ryan, 2026-09-03). Fe II <3D>-LTE IS available (model 5, the <3D>-mean atmosphere is ion-agnostic); model 5 == model 6 on Fe II by construction, which IS the phantom-departure check. This does NOT cover ENGINE-A: that leg reads the MPIA/Bergemann per-line grid, not this atom, and its Fe II corrections are real. RYA-1055.

body_html:
Fe.json v1.529 · 56 Fe II products · 266 total

Solar Fe I anchor: 7.477 ± 0.052

HARPS · Reference Grade · Amarsi 3D-NLTE · n = 21. The selected Fe I product anchors this Solar appendix; products and engines are not averaged together.

Highlighted band products

near-UV

7.671 ± 0.065

Kitt Peak · Synth · <3D>-LTE · Gerber · stagger · Reference Grade · n = 12

Uncertainty budget closed for six of eight rows (RYA-1226); two Fe I Kitt Peak/molecfit rows keep a legacy bar pending their microturbulence bracket. On the migrated rows most of the quoted systematic is a conservative profile-width term carried from a measurement in another band.

VIS

7.460 ± 0.100

Kitt Peak · Synth · 1D-LTE · Gerber · Reference Grade · n = 6

red-optical

7.346 ± 0.097

Kitt Peak · Synth · 1D-LTE · Gerber · Reference Grade · n = 1

Error-bar forest

How to read this forest. Each measured row is a separate abundance product for an instrument, holding, line pool and treatment; engines are never averaged together. Solid bars show statistical uncertainty from the line measurements; wireframes show systematic uncertainty from the product’s adopted error budget, which does not average away with more lines. Green and gold regions mark the Asplund and Lodders literature values and uncertainties, not pass/fail gates. Grades describe the line pool’s provenance and selection, not the quality of an engine. Reddish-orange mean-3D / Frankenstein rows are experimental and not adopted. Unmeasured model rows remain N/A.

Grades and model labels
  • Reference Grade. An externally published reference line pool, using that reference’s line selection and oscillator strengths; the current Fe reference products use AGSS21. This is a provenance category, not a promise that every line has an individual primary-laboratory uncertainty.
  • Deep Grade. The corresponding laboratory-data pool above that depth gate. These stronger lines extend coverage but require particular care with saturation and blends.

1D-LTE uses a one-dimensional atmosphere with atomic populations in local thermodynamic equilibrium. 1D-NLTE allows departures from that equilibrium; the named implementation supplies the correction or synthesis treatment.

Synthesis fits the spectral line profile. See Methodology for the full model, line-selection and uncertainty procedures.

Solar iron context

Fe II traces singly ionized iron and is retained as an ionization and consistency diagnostic alongside Fe I, not an independent headline to average with it. The current resolved pool contains strong, saturation-sensitive lines and documented blend exclusions; the diagnostics below distinguish those limitations from model and holding differences.

Near-UV opacity — report and noted

Molecular opacity INCLUDED — OH A-X, NH, CH and CN violet, 6,223 VALD lines as Turbospectrum lists with the dominant isotopologue (RYA-1207). The band previously carried none: every molecular list iSpec ships begins at 400 nm. Measured PAIRED against a molecules-off run on the same code and pool, the lever is -0.047..-0.055 dex on Fe I and -0.276..-0.332 on Fe II, with chi2r median 81.8 -> 67.4 and control windows containing no molecular line bit-identical. RYA-1209 additionally curated out Fe I 3721.272 (systematic:K07 — gf attributed to a VALD3 reference that publishes no per-line uncertainty, no NIST accuracy class, so it never met the DEEPGRADED tier's lab-gf definition); the Fe I pool is 57 candidates and the budget clears at gf rung 3 (cited lab), 55/55 GF-LAB, RMS 0.0509 dex. RESIDUAL DEFICIT: the correction still UNDER-corrects — RYA-1204 measured synth/obs above 1 on 24 of 40 windows after it — so the band remains short of opacity by an amount not yet measured on this pool, and these values are a floor rather than a converged answer. sigma_syst is unchanged at 0.1122 because it is dominated by the 0.10 dex pseudo-continuum term, not by gf: the true continuum is never observed here. Not adopted for the headline. The headline is the per-band best-available product, selected from this feed by the publication generator rather than fixed as a constant: RYA-850 promoted the graded laboratory-gf pool to the PRIMARY reported value, and RYA-819 retired the earlier constructed anchor after showing its Magic-2013 correction wrong in both magnitude and shape. RYA-161: nothing calibrated to a target.

Frankenstein — experimental, pending the Bride

2 experimental products remain available in the Fe I product values and downloads.

RYA-1197 Part A: the Frankenstein mean-<3D> route is HELD FROM HEADLINE publication until the Bride validates it. It inflates A(Fe) by roughly +0.10 dex against the 1D siblings and exists on VIS/KP only, so it is not a comparable measurement of the same quantity. It stays in the feed deliberately: the LTE/NLTE mean-3D PAIR is the NLTE differential on ONE atmosphere (RYA-542), which is the diagnostic it is for. Not a headline value.

Saturation characterization

Committed proof census: 120 line/holding records; 100% have observed depth > 0.70. Median observed log10(EW[mÅ]/λ[Å]) = -1.252. In consistent Å units this is -4.252. These diagnostics characterize the audited saturated pool, not every newly added product.
